archetypes.name: contract-drift
archetypes.rationale: Targets the live mismatch between Step 3 driver flags, loop argv contract, env-var docs, and skill invocation text.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether the plan's convergence-threshold removal reaches every contract boundary named in the staged files: skill invocation, driver usage and parsing, loop invocation, env-var docs, and structure tests. Look for stale references that would leave users, tests, or scripts believing the removed flag still exists, and for any planned edit that accidentally changes round-cap behavior. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: cleanup-fail-safe
archetypes.rationale: Focuses on the cleanup enumeration failure-path change and whether the proposed temp-file handling preserves existing deletion semantics.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the cleanup.sh portion of the plan against the current script behavior to verify that only top-level enumeration failure handling changes. Check whether the proposed mktemp and NUL-delimited read pattern preserves symlink exclusion, age gates, nested activity scanning, counts, and /tmp predicate asymmetry. Pay special attention to partial find output, temp-file cleanup, and Bash 3.2 compatibility. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: Checks whether the planned tests actually exercise the intended plan defects instead of only updating stale assertions.
archetypes.prompt_body: Inspect whether the proposed test updates would catch the two stated failures: silent top-level enumeration failure and Step 3 forwarding drift into plan-review-loop.sh. Compare the planned stubs and integration-seam test against the real scripts' option shapes so the tests fail for the right reasons and do not mask unrelated failures. Look for omitted existing harnesses or stale assertions that would keep CI red after the plan is implemented. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
